title: hotfix: fix connection leak in slo-enforcer during regional failover
author: Priya Desai
description: Background: During a regional failover stress test we observed a connection leak in the slo-enforcer that caused goroutines and file descriptors to accumulate when the regional routing layer retried requests. This manifested as degraded SLO enforcement throughput and, in one case, cascading load-shedding across regions. Motivation: This is a production-impacting reliability regression (ENG-9742) that requires an urgent hotfix to ensure graceful degradation and stable failover. Summary of changes: 1) Fix connection lifecycle in pkg/slo/enforcer: ensure per-request contexts are canceled and TCP connections are returned to the pool on both success and error paths. 2) Harden CB/fallback: add explicit cancelation hooks when regional failover starts to avoid dangling timers. 3) Add a new integration test that simulates regional failover under synthetic load to reproduce and prevent the leak. 4) Add an observability counter and alert for leaked connection counts to catch regressions early. Checklist: - [x] Reproduced leak locally with stress harness - [x] Added unit and integration tests - [x] CI passing (linux/unit + integration) - [x] Rollout plan documented in PR - [x] Feature flagged and gradual rollout to production Testing & validation: Local stress tests + integration test added (tests/slo-enforcer/connection_leak_test.go) that runs the failover loop for 60s and verifies no FD/goroutine growth. CI ran the full integration suite; a flaky test in routing was fixed in a follow-up commit. Rollout: Deploy to canary region (us-west-2) under feature flag slo_enforcer_connection_fix=false->true with 10% traffic for 30 minutes, monitor leaked_connection_count and SLO miss rate; if stable, promote to remaining regions. Related: references SUP-4210 for the customer incident and ENG-9742 for the engineering task.
